title: Direct and semi-direct aerosol radiative effect on the Mediterranean climate variability using a coupled regional climate system model
problem: Previous studies of aerosol climatic effects in the Mediterranean often neglect ocean-atmosphere coupling, preventing a full assessment of key feedback mechanisms where aerosol-induced changes in sea surface temperature modify regional climate.
method: This study uses a fully coupled regional climate system model (CNRM-RCSM4) to investigate the direct and semi-direct effects of aerosols on Mediterranean climate variability through multi-annual ensemble simulations with and without aerosol forcing and ocean-atmosphere coupling.
task: The task is to investigate the direct and semi-direct effects of aerosols on Mediterranean climate variability and ocean-atmosphere interactions using a coupled regional climate system model.

The present work has been carried out with the fully coupled regional climate system model developed at CNRM. It includes the regional climate atmospheric model ALADIN-Climate (Radu et al. 2008; Déqué and Somot 2008; Farda et al. 2010; Colin et al. 2010; Herrmann et al. 2011), the land-surface model ISBA (Noilhan and Mahfouf 1996), the river routing scheme TRIP (Decharme et al. 2010) and the regional ocean model NEMOMED8 (Beuvier et al. 2010).

ALADIN includes the Fouquart and Morcrette radiation scheme (FMR15, Morcrett 1989), based on the ECMWF model incorporating effects of greenhouse gases, direct effects of aerosols as well as the first indirect effect of sulfate aerosols (Twomey 1977).
It is a bi-spectral semi-implicit semilagrangian model, with a 50 km horizontal resolution.
This version has a horizontal resolution of 1/8°x 1/8°cos(lat), namely between 9 and 12 km, and 43 vertical levels, with layer thickness increasing from 6 m to 200 m.

A fully coupled regional climate system model (CNRM-RCSM4) has been used over the Mediterranean region to investigate the direct and semi-direct effects of aerosols, but also their role in the radiation-atmosphereocean interactions through multi-annual ensemble simulations (2003-2009) with and without aerosols and oceanatmosphere coupling.
Simulations have also been carried out without aerosols (C-NO), and with the atmospheric model only (F-AER with aerosols, and F-NO without aerosols).
